### Why Decode Throughput Tracks Weight-File Size in Bandwidth-Bound Mixture-of-Experts Models

In bandwidth-bound Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, **decode throughput**—the rate at which tokens can be generated during autoregressive inference—is tightly coupled to the **size of the weight file**, whereas **prefill throughput** (the initial processing of a prompt) is not. This divergence arises from differences in **arithmetic intensity** (the ratio of computation to data movement) between the two phases, and how the MoE architecture modifies this relationship when only a sparse subset of experts are active.

---

## 1. Arithmetic Intensity in Prefill vs. Decode

### 1.1. Arithmetic Intensity: A Brief Recap

Arithmetic intensity (AI) is defined as:

$$
\text{AI} = \frac{\text{FLOPs}}{\text{Bytes moved}}
$$

High AI implies computation-bound behavior (limited by compute), while low AI implies bandwidth-bound behavior (limited by memory bandwidth).

• The GB10 uses a unified memory architecture with a single 128 GB pool for weights, activations, and KV cache
• This eliminates the need to shuttle data across a bus between different memory types
• All three components (weights, activations, KV cache) share the same memory space
• Kernel-level bandwidth savings have system-wide impact, not just GPU-specific benefits
• The unified architecture fundamentally changes how model placement decisions are made

**What a CUDA kernel author should conclude:**

A CUDA kernel author should focus their optimization efforts on **bandwidth reduction techniques** since these will have cascading benefits across the entire system. In this unified memory architecture, every byte saved from memory bandwidth translates to system-wide efficiency gains rather than just GPU performance improvements. The author should prioritize:

1. **Memory access pattern optimization** - ensuring coalesced accesses and minimizing redundant reads/writes
2. **Cache-friendly algorithms** - leveraging the unified memory's ability to keep frequently accessed data readily available
3. **Kernel fusion strategies** - reducing intermediate memory operations between computational stages
4. **Data locality awareness** - structuring computations to maximize reuse of data already in the unified pool
